title: Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three
main_claim: There is N divisible by 8 and reduced real weighted-homogeneous polynomials f1,f2 in C^N with isolated singularities, ord f1=2, ord f2=3, whose hypersurface germs are ambiently homeomorphic. This answers the embedded Zariski multiplicity question negatively. Corollaries cover topological right equivalence, Arnold's corank problem, and the initial-form Milnor fibre conjecture of Budur–Fernández de Bobadilla–Lê–Nguyen.

issues.description: The integral monodromy-module isomorphism for Thom–Sebastiani sums of chains, including squares, the 5th/7th powers and 1-variable pure powers, depends on the cited scope of Hertling–Mase 2022 Thm 1.3(a),(c),(d). The paper converts conventions (reversed chain order, inverse monodromy) correctly, but I could not check against the source text that the theorem covers arbitrary TS sums of chain type.
issues.evidence: background.tex: 'The precise result used here is [HertlingMase2022, Theorem 1.3(a),(c),(d), and Definition 2.6]'. Used without further argument in seeds.tex and Cor seed:prepared.

coverage: I read all sections (background, seeds, local, global, conclusion, certificate) in full and checked the steps line by line. I ran both verification scripts: the rank certificate passes silently, and the explicit relation check passed (849 terms, positive sum, chain and dimension checks). Python checks: the cotangent triple-angle identity (seed:cotangent) for random odd k with 3∤k and admissible b (max relative error 9e-12); the Case 1 exceptional values (1-w)/w and their reduction to A_b and R_b/A_b; the Case 3 cube character value 0. By hand I checked: B=ST^r is symmetric and T-invariant (uses 2r≡1 mod m); T^tST=S; the odd-prime square-root and two-squares lifting and the Frobenius-conjugate argument; the off-diagonal M^*M=diag(U,U); the dyadic unramified hermitian diagonalization and norm surjectivity; the Hasse descent through hermitian length forms; the reverser algebra C^tSC=S^t ⇒ C^{-1}TC=T^{-1}, C^tBC=B, including linking signs for even s; the determinant cancellation ∏ t_γ^{m_η} t_η^{-m_γ}=1 on each eigenspace; the six-cube data S_u=-A^{⊗6}, t, J=At^2, the lengths 27(-1)^{k+1} and signatures (20,2) and (6,15); the identification of G as a product of SU groups and the hypotheses of strong approximation; the adelic-to-integral lattice step; det(1-T)=1 via Φ_d(1)=1 for 143|d; Wang sequence, Alexander duality, Hurewicz and Smale; the hypotheses of Levine's theorem; the weighted cone homeomorphism; and the Saeki/King conjugation removal by real coefficients. I took the classical cited theorems (Nemethi real Seifert form, Hertling–Mase, Platonov, Levine) on citation after checking their stated hypotheses.
